newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger amid sharp U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger amid sharp U.S. gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Monday, rallying with U.S. treasuries after the release of weaker than expected U.S. economic data, analysts said.

"We had basically a technical rally. I think most chartists had buy signals last Friday and they were just confirmed early this morning," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc. "We shot off with the U.S."
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.67 to C$109.85 to yield 7.162 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 19/32 to yield 6.74 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 43 basis points from 42 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
Both Canadian and U.S. bond markets rallied after a report this morning that the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Managers index fell to 52.0 in January from a revised 53.8 in December.
"It indicated that the rate of growth was slowing down just a tad," said Dong. "I think people were looking for an excuse to keep on buying this market," he said.

Both Canadian and U.S. bond investors are now looking ahead to the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday. While recent U.S. economic data has shown that inflation there remains subdued, there is the risk that the Fed could hike rates to prevent a rise inflation, analysts said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.47 to C$103.75 to yield 6.476 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 12/32 to yield 6.45 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds was three basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.84 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.11 percent.
